body:
Closes #7857

A function that reaches its error label with no exception set segfaults on Python 3.12+:

```cython
cdef int f(int x) except -1:
    return x

def trigger():
    f(-1)
```

`__Pyx_AddTraceback` ends in `PyTraceBack_Here()`, which since 3.12 takes the raised exception and reads its traceback without checking for NULL. Before 3.12 it was NULL tolerant, and the caller later got CPython's "returned NULL without setting an exception" instead.

As da-woods said on the issue this is mostly a user error, but it's on the slow error path so a check costs nothing. `__Pyx_AddTraceback` now sets `SystemError("error return without exception set")` if nothing is set, which is the same message CPython's eval loop uses for this case. It's done in both the regular and the Limited API version and on all Python versions, so the error and the traceback look the same everywhere. The traceback points at the function that took the error path.

One limitation: the exception only exists once the function is on its way out, so an `except SystemError` around the call in the same function won't catch it. A caller one level up does.

The new test crashes on master (3.12, 3.14 and Limited API) and passes with the change on 3.11, 3.12, 3.14 and with `--limited-api=3.12`. The `traceback`, `except` and `generator_frame` test patterns also pass.

Generators and coroutines don't go through this path. Their error label only calls `__Pyx_AddTraceback` when an exception is set, so a generator just stops, and an `async def` crashes inside asyncio's task step because the send returns an error with nothing set. I left that alone here, happy to look at it separately.

comment_data.body: It seems like it should probably be possible to avoid the call to `PyErr_Occurred()` (definitely in the Limited API case, and probably in the regular case)

commit.message: Raise SystemError instead of crashing on an error return without exception
Shorten test name to make it reusable for future additions in the same context.
